newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-Coffee set to consolidate in lower range.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Coffee set to consolidate in lower range.

text.p: SEPT Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Robusta coffee futures should consolidate in a lower range after last week's sell-off but key September still has a series of support points before $1,500 a tonne, technical analysts said on Monday.
London reversed an earlier weaker trend to end Friday higher, but well below the day's peaks on late selling in a thin session.
Traders called the market to open $25 lower than Friday's close.
"It's broken down but now it seems to be holding again in a new range between $1,530 and $1,700," said Adrian Haylor, a technical analyst at Sucden.
"It all looks rather dull...it's finding a new lower range," he said.
On the upside, resistance was pegged at $1,645 followed by $1,695 and $1,750. Support was at $1,570, $1,530 and $1,500.
Fundamental news was thin on the ground, with few new developments expected in the Brazil weather pattern.

According to local meteorologists Somar, the country's coffee regions will continue to see mild temperatures throughout this week with no threatening polar air mass forecast seen in the seven-day outlook.
A cold front will pass through north Parana state on Monday, spreading to south Minas Gerais on Tuesday but will bring only scattered showers, it said.

Complete Coffee Coverage reported U.S. green coffee roastings at an approximate total of 285,000 60-kg bags for the week ended July 12, up from 195,000 bags the previous week. -- Jeremy Smith, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8064
